title: End-to-End Evaluation Plan for the Page Optimization Result
title_zh: 页面优化结果端到端评估方案
goal: End-to-end evaluation of the optimization result across two independent lenses: (A) objective scoring (deterministic, reproducible, no LLM) and (B) agent subjective scoring (LLM-as-judge, rubric-based). Combine both into a single final score + PASS/FAIL/REVIEW verdict.
constraints: a14y before/after comparison must use PAGE-LEVEL checks only; exclude siteChecks (robots.txt/llms.txt/sitemap/AGENTS.md) because the tool optimizes a single page, not the site (README note #7).

Do NOT do byte-level diffing: the optimizer re-serializes HTML via BeautifulSoup (tag lower-casing, double-quoting, entity encoding, self-closing voids), so structural/text-semantic comparison is required instead (README note #9).
Content integrity is a HARD GATE: any loss of original URLs, fabricated content, or significant text change invalidates the whole result regardless of scores.
Subjective judge must be framed neutrally (compare two versions of the same page) and, when possible, use a different model than the generator to reduce self-preference bias.

part_a_objective_scoring.description: Deterministic, reproducible, no LLM required. Three sub-metrics -> one objective score.

a1_a14y_score.method: run `a14y check <url> -o json -m page` against the original page and the optimized page (served via a local http.server); extract per-page summary.score and per-check statuses.
a1_a14y_score.scope: PAGE-LEVEL only: use pages[].summary.score and pages[].checks; ignore the top-level siteChecks.

a2_content_integrity.description: HARD GATE. Re-verify independently (port logic from optimize_page.py helpers _parse/_urls, not just trusting its self_check).

urls_preserved.method: set(original_urls) subset of set(optimized_urls), after HTML-entity decoding of href/src/action/iframe-src

text_preserved.method: strip tags, normalize whitespace, compare original vs optimized body text via difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio (or char-level similarity)

no_fabricated_content.method: no new <a> links, no new <nav>/<footer> blocks, no new .css/.js resource references not present in source

a2_content_integrity.score_formula: integrity_score = 0.3*(100 if urls_preserved else 0) + 0.4*(text_similarity*100) + 0.3*(100 if no_fabricated else 0)

a3_structural_metadata.description: Checklist of structural/metadata items the optimizer is expected to deliver (total = 100 points).

part_a_objective_scoring.hard_gate: if NOT urls_preserved OR text_similarity < 0.95 OR NOT no_fabricated_content -> objective_verdict = FAIL (overrides everything)

part_b_subjective_scoring.description: LLM-as-judge, rubric-based quality scoring on a 1-5 scale (5 = best). Each dimension requires a score + one-line justification.

judge_dimensions.label: Do title / meta description / og tags accurately and concisely reflect the page content, with no hallucinated facts?
Is the meaning and information content preserved (nothing important added, removed, or changed)?
How much clearer / more AI-readable is the optimized page than the original?
Is the injected design system appropriate, consistent, responsive, and non-destructive to existing styles?
Is the JSON-LD semantically correct and grounded in real page content (not fabricated)?
Holistic judgment: would you ship this optimized page as-is?

procedure.judge_model: from llm_config.json (strong model preferred); ideally DIFFERENT from the generator model to reduce self-preference bias
procedure.framing: neutral: 'compare two versions of the same page' (blind, no mention of which tool produced them)
procedure.input: original page text + optimized page text side by side (extracted readable text, not raw bytes)
procedure.reliability: compute mean and std per dimension across the 3 runs; flag any dimension with std >= 1.0 for human review

part_b_subjective_scoring.aggregation: subjective_score_1to5 = mean over dimensions of (per-dimension mean); subjective_score_0to100 = subjective_score_1to5 * 20

verdict_rules.REVIEW: otherwise (meets part but not all thresholds, or high judge variance)

part_c_final_aggregation.weights_note: 0.6/0.4 and all thresholds are defaults; store them in a single config block so they can be tuned per run

steps.title: Preparation & prerequisite checks
steps.goal: Confirm inputs exist and tooling is available before scoring.
steps.method: Verify original_page and optimized_page exist; verify `a14y` on PATH (npm install -g a14y); verify llm_config.json has a key for the judge stage; start a local http.server to expose both HTML files as URLs.

steps.title: Objective — a14y score before/after (page-level)
steps.goal: Capture the authoritative before/after AI-readability score and the exact checks that flipped.
steps.method: Run `a14y check <url> -o json -m page` for before and after; extract pages[].summary.score and diff pages[].checks statuses; ignore siteChecks.

steps.title: Objective — content integrity (hard gate)
steps.goal: Prove the optimizer did not lose URLs, change meaning, or fabricate content.
steps.method: Independently re-verify: URL set inclusion (entity-decoded), normalized text similarity (difflib), and absence of new <a>/<nav>/<footer> and new .css/.js. Reuse optimize_page._parse / _urls.

steps.title: Objective — structural & metadata completeness
steps.goal: Verify the expected structural/metadata deliverables are all present and valid.
steps.method: Parse the optimized page with BeautifulSoup and score the 12-item checklist (part_a.a3_structural_metadata.items), including JSON-LD validity and text-ratio improvement vs the original.

steps.title: Objective — compute objective score
steps.goal: Combine A1/A2/A3 into one objective score and verdict.
steps.method: Apply objective_formula; then apply hard_gate to set objective_verdict.

steps.title: Subjective — build judge prompt & rubric
steps.goal: Prepare a neutral, deterministic judge prompt with the 6-dimension rubric.
steps.method: Render the 6 judge_dimensions into a system prompt; extract readable text from original + optimized pages; add forced-JSON output instruction and 1-5 anchors.

steps.title: Subjective — run the judge (N runs)
steps.goal: Collect N independent judgments for reliability.
steps.method: Call the judge model 3 times (temperature 0.7), parse each forced-JSON response, and validate every dimension has an integer score 1-5.

steps.title: Subjective — aggregate
steps.goal: Turn N judgments into one subjective score with reliability flags.
steps.method: Per dimension compute mean and std across the 3 runs; subjective_score_1to5 = mean over dimensions; flag dimensions with std >= 1.0.

steps.title: Final aggregation & verdict
steps.goal: Merge objective and subjective into a single end-to-end result.

steps.title: Report generation
steps.goal: Persist everything in machine-readable + human-readable form.
steps.method: Write evaluation_report.json (all raw metrics, flips, per-dimension rubric, final score, verdict) and evaluation_report.md (before/after scores, flips, integrity pass/fail, rubric table, final score + verdict + recommended follow-ups).

reuse_existing: ai_eval.py can produce the a14y scorecard + LLM analysis for each side if a full narrative is wanted
optimize_page.self_check() already covers a subset of A2/A3 — the evaluator should re-verify independently rather than trust it
